claim: A self-driving car is capable of operating with reduced or no human input.
quote: A self-driving car...is a car that is capable of operating with reduced or no human input.

claim: The term 'self-driving' lacks an agreed standard definition as of 2026.
quote: As of 2026, the term 'self-driving' lacks an agreed standard definition.

claim: Self-driving cars are sometimes called robotaxis when operated for ridesharing.
quote: They are sometimes called robotaxis, though this term refers specifically to self-driving cars operated for a ridesharing company.

claim: No system has achieved full autonomy in all domains, referred to as 'Level 5'.
quote: no system has achieved full autonomy in all domains - sometimes referred to as 'Level 5'.

claim: LiDAR and visual sensors are primary technologies used in self-driving cars.
quote: two main technologies are now primarily used: LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging), and visual sensors (cameras).

claim: Public acceptance of autonomous cars is influenced by 'self-AV bias'.
quote: Public acceptance is also influenced by 'self-AV bias'.

claim: Wayve Technologies Ltd is a British company focused on developing autonomous driving systems using end-to-end deep learning.
quote: Wayve Technologies Ltd is a British autonomous driving technology company focused on developing self-driving vehicle systems through end-to-end deep learning.

claim: Wayve's approach to autonomous driving avoids detailed 3D maps and hand-coded rules, using a self-learning AI driver instead.
quote: Wayve’s approach eschews detailed 3D maps and hand-coded rules, in favour of a self-learning "AI driver".

claim: Wayve's autonomous vehicles operate using camera data and machine learning algorithms, without relying on lidar sensors.
quote: Wayve’s platform learns to drive predominantly using camera data and machine learning algorithms.

claim: Wayve's AI-driven driving software is referred to as an "Embodied AI" or AI Driver.
quote: The company refers to its AI-driven driving software as an “Embodied AI” or AI Driver.

claim: Wayve's autonomy stack is hardware-agnostic and consists of video cameras and basic automotive sensors.
quote: The Wayve hardware-agnostic autonomy stack consists of a suite of video cameras, with basic automotive sensors.

claim: Wayve plans to license its AI technology to established automakers rather than build its own cars.
quote: Wayve’s strategy is to provide its driving AI as an OEM-ready platform; it plans to license or embed its technology into vehicles made by established automakers.

claim: Mobile robotics is a subfield of robotics and information engineering.
quote: Mobile robotics is usually considered to be a subfield of robotics and information engineering.

claim: Autonomous mobile robots can navigate uncontrolled environments without guidance devices.
quote: Mobile robots can be "autonomous" (AMR - autonomous mobile robot) which means they are capable of navigating an uncontrolled environment without the need for physical or electro-mechanical guidance devices.

claim: Mobile robots are used in commercial, industrial, military, and security settings.
quote: Mobile robots are also found in industrial, military and security settings.

claim: Mobile robots consist of a controller, sensors, actuators, and a power system.
quote: The components of a mobile robot are a controller, sensors, actuators and power system.

claim: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) describes wireless communication between a vehicle and any entity that may affect, or may be affected by, the vehicle.
quote: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) describes wireless communication between a vehicle and any entity that may affect, or may be affected by, the vehicle.

claim: V2X is intended to improve road safety and traffic efficiency while reducing pollution and saving energy.
quote: it is a vehicular communication system that is intended to improve road safety and traffic efficiency while reducing pollution and saving energy.

claim: There are two standards for dedicated V2X communications: WLAN-based and cellular-based.
quote: There are two standards for dedicated V2X communications depending on the underlying wireless technology being used: (1) WLAN-based, and (2) cellular-based.

claim: Vehicle-to-device (V2D) involves Bluetooth or WiFi-Direct communication, such as Apple's CarPlay and Google's Android Auto.
quote: Vehicle-to-device (V2D) - Bluetooth / WiFi-Direct, e.g. Apple's CarPlay and Google's Android Auto.

claim: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) involves information exchange with the smart grid to balance loads more efficiently.
quote: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) - information exchange with the smart grid to balance loads more efficiently.

claim: Vehicle-to-network (V2N) involves communication between a vehicle and a wider network, such as a cellular network.
quote: Vehicle-to-network (V2N) - communication between a vehicle and a wider network, such as a cellular network.

claim: Vehicle-to-cloud (V2C) includes OTA updates and remote vehicle diagnostics.
quote: Vehicle-to-cloud (V2C) - e.g. OTA updates, remote vehicle diagnostics (DoIP).

claim: Vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) involves communication with traffic lights, lane markers, and parking meters.
quote: Vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) - e.g. traffic lights, lane markers and parking meters.

claim: Vehicle-to-pedestrian (V2P) communication is used for wheelchairs and bicycles, designating vulnerable road users (VRUs).
quote: Vehicle-to-pedestrian (V2P) - e.g. wheelchairs and bicycles, commonly also used to designate vulnerable road users (VRUs).

claim: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) involves real-time data exchange with nearby vehicles.
quote: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) - real-time data exchange with nearby vehicles.

claim: Lane departure warning systems (LDWS) are designed to warn drivers when a vehicle begins to move out of its lane.
quote: a lane departure warning system ( LDWS ) is a mechanism designed to warn the driver when the vehicle begins to move out of its lane.

claim: Lane departure warning systems aim to minimize accidents caused by driver error, distractions, and drowsiness.
quote: These systems are designed to minimize accidents by addressing the main causes of collisions: driver error, distractions and drowsiness.

claim: Lane departure warning systems use video, laser, and infrared sensors to detect lane departures.
quote: Lane warning/keeping systems are based on: Video sensors... Laser sensors... Infrared sensors...

claim: Lane keeping assist systems can automatically take steps to keep a vehicle in its lane if the driver does not respond to warnings.
quote: Lane keeping assist (LKA/LKS): Systems which warn the driver and, with no response, automatically take steps to ensure the vehicle stays in its lane.

claim: Lane centering assist systems help keep the car centered in the lane and prompt the driver to take over in challenging situations.
quote: Lane centering assist (LCA): Systems which assist in oversteering, keeping the car centered in the lane, and asking the driver to take over in challenging situations.

claim: Automated lane keeping systems (ALKS) are designed to follow lane markings without human intervention.
quote: Automated lane keeping systems (ALKS): Designed to follow lane markings with no human driver.

claim: Emergency lane keeping systems apply corrections when a vehicle drifts beyond a solid lane marking.
quote: The emergency lane keeping applies correction to a vehicle which drifts beyond a solid lane marking.

claim: Lane detection systems use Hough transform and Canny edge detector to identify lane lines from camera images.
quote: A lane detection system used behind the lane departure warning system uses the principle of Hough transform and Canny edge detector to detect lane lines.

claim: Lane departure warning systems do not function if lane edges are not marked by lines.
quote: This system does not work when the edge of the lane is not marked by a line.

claim: Cruise LLC was acquired by General Motors in 2016 and focused on producing a fleet of driverless taxis.
quote: The company was acquired by General Motors in 2016, and operated as a largely autonomous subsidiary, focusing on producing a fleet of driverless taxis.

claim: Cruise initially developed direct-to-consumer kits for retrofitting vehicles with limited self-driving capabilities.
quote: Cruise initially focused on developing direct-to-consumer kits to retrofit vehicles with limited self-driving capabilities.

claim: Cruise received a permit to test self-driving vehicle technology from the California DMV in June 2015.
quote: Cruise received a permit to test self-driving vehicle technology from the California Department of Motor Vehicles in June 2015.

claim: Cruise forms the core of GM's self-driving efforts.
quote: Cruise forms the core of GM's self-driving efforts.

claim: In September 2021, Cruise received a permit to provide driverless taxi rides in California without safety drivers.
quote: In September 2021, Cruise received a permit from the California Department of Motor Vehicles to provide driverless taxi rides in the state.

claim: Cruise announced plans to expand its service to Phoenix, Arizona, and Austin, Texas, in September 2022.
quote: In September 2022, the company announced it would expand its service to Phoenix, Arizona, and Austin, Texas, within three months.

claim: Cruise's operations were suspended in October 2023 following safety concerns and incidents.
quote: In October 2023, following a barrage of safety concerns and incidents...the California DMV suspended Cruise's self-driving car permits.

claim: Vehicular automation involves using technology to assist or replace the operator of a vehicle.
quote: Vehicular automation is using technology to assist or replace the operator of a vehicle such as a car, truck, aircraft, rocket, military vehicle, or boat.

claim: Autonomous vehicles are responsible for all perception, monitoring, and control functions.
quote: Autonomy implies that the vehicle is responsible for all perception, monitoring, and control functions.

claim: The SAE classification of levels is based on the role of the driver, not the vehicle's capabilities.
quote: The SAE classification of levels is based on the role of the driver, rather than the vehicle's capabilities.

claim: Autonomous vehicle software includes perception, localization, and planning modules.
quote: Autonomous vehicle software generally contains several different modules that work together to enable self-driving capabilities.

claim: The perception module processes data from sensors like cameras, LIDAR, RADAR, and SONAR.
quote: The perception module ingests and processes data from various sensors, such cameras , LIDAR , RADAR , and ultrasonic SONAR.

claim: Navigation systems are essential for autonomous vehicles, using GPS for navigation.
quote: Navigation systems are a necessary element in autonomous vehicles. The Global Positioning System (GPS) is used for navigation.

claim: Sensor fusion techniques improve accuracy and reliability in autonomous driving systems.
quote: modern autonomous driving systems increasingly employ sensor fusion techniques that combine data from multiple sensors to improve accuracy and reliability.

claim: The Stanford Cart was the first experimental autonomous vehicle, developed in the late 1970s.
quote: The "Stanford Cart", created by Hans Moravec in the late 1970s...was the first experimental autonomous vehicle.

claim: Automated vehicles in EU legislation refer specifically to road vehicles like cars, trucks, or buses.
quote: Automated vehicles in European Union legislation refer specifically to road vehicles (car, truck, or bus).

claim: The SAfe Road TRains for the Environment (Sartre) project aimed to enable platooning of vehicles.
quote: The SAfe Road TRains for the Environment (Sartre) project's goal was to enable platooning, in which a line of cars and trucks (a "train") follow a human-driven vehicle.

claim: Autonomous aircraft operate without human intervention using on-board robotic systems.
quote: An autonomous aircraft is an aircraft which flies under the control of on-board autonomous robotic systems and needs no intervention from a human pilot or remote control.

claim: Most autonomous aircraft are unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with pre-programmed algorithms.
quote: Most contemporary autonomous aircraft are unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) with pre-programmed algorithms to perform designated tasks.

claim: Autonomous aircraft are reaching a point where air taxis and regulatory regimes are being developed.
quote: autonomous control systems are reaching a point where several air taxis and associated regulatory regimes are being developed.

claim: Autonomous aircraft development includes air taxis and larger autonomous transports.
quote: A number of air taxis are under development and larger autonomous transports are also being planned.

claim: Degrees of freedom (DOF) in UAVs refer to the amount and quality of sensors on board.
quote: Degrees of freedom (DOF) refers to both the amount and quality of sensors on board.

claim: UAVs use open-loop, closed-loop, or hybrid control architectures for operation.
quote: UAVs employ open-loop, closed-loop or hybrid control architectures.

claim: UAVs rely on single-board computers for computational needs due to real-time system requirements.
quote: UAVs are real-time systems that require rapid response to changing sensor data. As a result, UAVs rely on single-board computers for their computational needs.

claim: The MAVLink protocol is popular for command and control data between ground control and UAVs.
quote: The MAVLink protocol is increasingly becoming popular to carry command and control data between the ground control and the vehicle.

claim: Autonomous robots can operate without human control, including examples like self-driving vacuums and cars.
quote: An autonomous robot is a robot that acts without recourse to human control. Historic examples include space probes . Modern examples include self-driving vacuums and cars .

claim: Industrial robot arms are considered autonomous but have restricted autonomy due to structured environments.
quote: Industrial robot arms that work on assembly lines inside factories may also be considered autonomous robots, though their autonomy is restricted due to a highly structured environment and their inability to locomote .

claim: Proprioception is a key component of robotic autonomy, allowing robots to sense their internal status.
quote: Self-maintenance is based on " proprioception ", or sensing one's own internal status.

claim: Exteroception involves sensing environmental factors, crucial for autonomous robot operation.
quote: Exteroception is sensing things about the environment. Autonomous robots must have a range of environmental sensors to perform their task and stay out of trouble.

claim: Autonomous robots use various sensors for localization and navigation, adapting to different environments.
quote: The most advanced systems now fuse information from various sensors for both localization (position) and navigation.

claim: Outdoor autonomy is challenging for ground vehicles due to surface density disparities and environmental instability.
quote: Outdoor autonomy is the most difficult for ground vehicles, due to: Great disparities in surface density Instability of the sensed environment

claim: Autonomous robots face challenges like systemic robustness and real-world brittleness due to environmental changes.
quote: Autonomous robots remain highly vulnerable to unexpected changes in real-world environments.

claim: Unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) operate without an onboard human presence and can be remote-operated or autonomous.
quote: An unmanned ground vehicle ( UGV )...is a vehicle that operates while in contact with the ground without an onboard human presence.

claim: UGVs are used in situations where it is inconvenient, dangerous, expensive, or impossible to use an onboard human operator.
quote: UGVs can be used for many applications where it is inconvenient, dangerous, expensive, or impossible to use an onboard human operator.

claim: UGVs are the land-based counterparts to unmanned aerial, underwater, and surface vehicles.
quote: The UGV is the land-based counterpart to unmanned aerial vehicles , unmanned underwater vehicles and unmanned surface vehicles.

claim: UGVs generally include a vehicle platform, sensors, control systems, guidance interface, communication links, and systems integration features.
quote: UGVs generally include: a vehicle platform , sensors , control systems , guidance interface, communication links, and systems integration features.

claim: UGVs can be powered by internal combustion engines, batteries, or hydrogen.
quote: Power sources can be internal combustion engines , batteries, or hydrogen.

claim: Remote-operated UGVs are controlled by a human operator using direct visual observation or sensors.
quote: A remote-operated UGV is controlled by a human operator. The operator makes decisions based upon either direct visual observation or sensors such as cameras.

claim: An autonomous UGV replaces the human controller with AI technologies and uses sensors to model the environment.
quote: An autonomous UGV (AGV) is an autonomous robot that replaces the human controller with artificial intelligence technologies.

claim: UGVs must navigate based on maps, detect objects, travel between waypoints, and avoid harm unless part of their mission.
quote: An autonomous vehicle must have the ability to: Navigate based on maps...Detect objects...Travel between waypoints...Avoid harming people, property or itself.
